method: Claude independent reading of PDFs (uploaded directly), blind to Themis output
notes: Clause types use the 16-type extract taxonomy. Risk flags are Claude's own judgment of deal risk.

lease_01_office_meridian.title: Office lease, Oakmont Realty Trust (Landlord) / Cobalt Industries, Inc. (Tenant), 10-year term, 220 Ridgeline Plaza
risk_flags: Rent is payable 'without deduction, offset, or counterclaim' except as expressly permitted, limiting Tenant's self-help remedies for Landlord non-performance.
Landlord has no duty to mitigate damages beyond what applicable law requires, increasing Tenant's exposure on default.
Casualty termination right in Art6.2 is framed as Landlord's unilateral option, with no corresponding Tenant termination right disclosed in this section.
HVAC rider is incorporated by reference (Art8.1) but its terms are not reproduced in the body of this document, creating an incorporation-by-reference blind spot.
No late-payment/interest clause was identified in the reviewed sections, so cost of a late payment default is not quantifiable from this excerpt.

lease_02_retail_sundial.title: Retail lease, Sundial Business Park LLC (Party A/Landlord) / Brightwell Logistics (Party B/Tenant), 7-year term
risk_flags: No explicit Tenant termination right is stated if compulsory reconstruction (Section7.1) takes an extended period, unlike leases with a reconstruction-duration exit right.
Extension-period rent is set by good-faith negotiation falling back to arbitration (Section3.3), creating renewal rent uncertainty rather than a fixed formula.
Landlord's Section6.2 code-compliance warranty is qualified 'to its knowledge,' materially weakening the representation Tenant can rely on.
Service Charges/CAM obligations (Section5.1) carry no stated annual cap, exposing Tenant to uncapped operating-cost pass-throughs.
The go-dark right (Section2) is favorable to Tenant but should be cross-checked against any co-tenancy or percentage-rent provisions elsewhere in the full lease not included here.

lease_03_industrial_ferrous.title: Industrial lease, Ferrous Manufacturing Co. (Lessor) / Northgate Ventures (Lessee), 8-year term
risk_flags: Reinstatement of the Lease after a default-and-cure (ArtVII.1) is at Lessor's 'sole discretion,' giving Tenant no guaranteed right to reinstate even after curing.
Holdover rent jumps immediately to 150% of Base Rent with no grace period (ArtIII.1), a materially punitive overstay penalty.
Change-of-control consent is triggered at a 50% equity-transfer threshold (ArtVI.1), which may restrict routine Tenant financing or ownership restructuring.
Right of First Refusal to purchase is a valuable Tenant right but is silent on what happens if Lessor's initial notice terms are later amended before closing.
Indemnification obligation (ArtVIII.2) runs one-way from Lessee to Lessor with no reciprocal Lessor indemnity disclosed in this section.

lease_03_industrial_ferrous_SCANNED.title: Scanned/rasterized counterpart of the Ferrous Manufacturing / Northgate Ventures industrial lease (image-only PDF, no embedded text layer)
risk_flags: Document is an image-only scan (no embedded text layer, rasterized with added noise/rotation/blur); clause text was reconstructed from the known source and should be re-verified against actual OCR output before production use.

Same substantive risks as the clean version apply: sole-discretion reinstatement (ArtVII.1), immediate 150% holdover penalty (ArtIII.1), 50%-threshold change-of-control consent (ArtVI.1), and one-way indemnity (ArtVIII.2).

Scan artifacts (skew, contrast drift, scan-line banding) increase the risk of OCR misreads on numeric values (e.g., the 150% holdover multiplier or the 50% control threshold) — these figures warrant manual confirmation.

lease_04_mixeduse_silverline.title: Mixed-use lease, Silverline Capital Partners (Landlord) / Aurelia Systems Inc. (Tenant), 700 Meridian Avenue
risk_flags: Jury trial waiver (Art7.1) removes Tenant's access to a jury in any Lease-related litigation.
Landlord disclaims liability for theft or vandalism of Tenant's property (Art7.2), shifting security-related loss risk entirely to Tenant.
HVAC warranty runs only 90 days from Commencement Date (Art3.3); after that, HVAC repair costs likely fall under Tenant's general maintenance obligation.
Landlord's condemnation and code-related representations are made only 'as of the date of this Lease' (Art3.2), giving no ongoing warranty for later-arising issues.

Change-of-control provision (Art5) gives Landlord a termination right, not just a consent right, if a Change of Control results in a Competing Business operating the Premises — a stronger-than-usual Landlord remedy.

lease_05_smallsuite_thornfield.title: Small-suite lease, Thornfield Group (Landlord) / Ridgeline Holdings (Tenant), 5-year term, no numbered clause headings
risk_flags: This lease uses prose headings rather than numbered clauses/articles, which increases the risk of ambiguous cross-referencing in disputes or amendments.
The 'Riders' section incorporates a Special Stipulations Rider by reference without reproducing its terms — the actual termination-right details it grants are not visible in this document.
Break option requires notice 9 months before the 36-month mark with a fee of 3 months' rent; a narrow, easy-to-miss exercise window given the lack of numbered clause tracking.
'Any ambiguity...shall not be construed against the drafting party' (Miscellaneous) waives Tenant's benefit of the contra proferentem interpretation rule.
Specialized cleaning charges beyond standard janitorial (Services) are billed separately with no stated cap.

lease_05_smallsuite_thornfield_SCANNED.title: Scanned/rasterized counterpart of the Thornfield Group / Ridgeline Holdings small-suite lease (image-only PDF, no embedded text layer)
risk_flags: Document is an image-only scan (no embedded text layer, rasterized with added noise/rotation/blur); clause text was reconstructed from the known source and should be re-verified against actual OCR output before production use.
Same substantive risks as the clean version apply: unreproduced Rider terms, narrow break-option exercise window, and waived contra proferentem protection.
Absence of clause numbering combined with scan noise compounds cross-reference risk — an OCR error on a heading could cause a section to be silently mis-associated in downstream parsing.

lease_06_table_rentschedule_bellwood.title: Lease with embedded rent-schedule and operating-expense tables, Bellwood Enterprises (Landlord) / Meridian Retail LLC (Tenant)
risk_flags: The Base Rent Schedule table shows compounding annual increases (~3% year-over-year) that cumulate to roughly a 19% increase by Lease Year 7 — Tenant should model total cost of occupancy across the full term, not just Year 1 rent.

Operating Expense table shows Tenant's Proportionate Share fixed at 9.6% with no stated cap on year-over-year growth in underlying expense categories (CAM, taxes, insurance, utilities, security), exposing Tenant to uncapped pass-through cost growth.
Tenant's audit right (Art3.3) is limited to once per calendar year, which could delay resolution of a disputed expense reconciliation.
Late fee is set at 5% of any late installment (Art4.1), a relatively high rate worth confirming against jurisdictional caps on late-fee/interest provisions.
This document is a strong test of table-extraction robustness — verify the model does not misclassify numeric table rows as free-text deontic clauses.

lease_07_edgecase_stresstest_windmere.title: Edge-case stress-test lease, Windmere Capital (Landlord) / Halcyon Foods Inc. (Tenant) — deliberately dense in ambiguous/compound clauses
risk_flags: Art1.3 waives Tenant's right to offset Rent 'regardless of the merits of any such claim' — a broad, unconditional waiver that removes a key tenant self-help remedy even for undisputed Landlord breaches.
Art1.2 (no duty to relet in preference) combined with Art1.3 (offset waiver) compounds Tenant's exposure: Tenant has limited recourse if Landlord underperforms on reletting or other obligations.
Art4.2's TI allowance forfeiture is triggered by failing to commence construction within just 90 days — an aggressive, easy-to-miss deadline with a full-forfeiture (not pro-rata) consequence.

Art4.3 gives Landlord broad discretion ('shall be entitled to require') to demand a replacement guaranty or increased deposit upon a Guarantor net-worth decline, with no defined process, notice period, or Tenant cure right specified.
Art4.1 percentage rent above the Breakpoint has no stated ceiling, so Tenant's rent exposure scales uncapped with Gross Sales performance.

Several clauses (Art2.1, Art2.3, Art3.1, Art3.2) combine a restriction and a carve-out permission within a single sentence — this compound structure is a known source of misclassification risk for automated clause-type/deontic classifiers and merits manual double-check regardless of model output.
